text.suptitle: Is output-ness a continuous property or a binary one?
fig_texts: TOP ROW: full-dictionary density of each continuous measure — needs no $R^2$, so these verdicts are DEFINITIVE.   BOTTOM ROW: median $R^2$ per decile — PROVISIONAL TARGET — #1738 SAE->SAE context arm. The correct target (full-width dense->SAE, task #7) does not exist yet. The two arms rank features at rho = 0.933 at panel width, so SHAPE conclusions survive the swap; LEVELS do not.

dashed vertical = the q0.90 cut the binary promoting/suppressing class uses; dotted verticals = detected KDE modes. A unimodal density with the cut inside the bulk means the binary class is a slice off a continuum, not a natural kind.

axes.xlabel: decile of positive-logit mass on top-10 tokens

axes.title_left: step-like, but the step is NOT at the q0.90 cut
